qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A hit documentary about home recording swept streaming services, music-production videos drew millions of views, and 'producer' became the career every teenager mentioned. Yet the professional software still cost nine hundred dollars a license, and studio-grade equipment still ran thousands, leaving actual production as far out of reach for most people as ever. Which phrase best describes what happened to music production?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: It became more exclusive than before.

qti-content-body.p: Exactly. The documentary spread the fame and appeal of music production -- millions of views, every teenager talking about it -- while the price of actually doing it never budged. Spreading something's fame and appeal is popularization; a pastime can be popularized and still stay too expensive for most people to try.

Track what changed and what didn't. Interest in producing music exploded, but the nine-hundred-dollar software and the thousands-of-dollars equipment stayed exactly where they were -- so access neither narrowed, nor opened up, nor fell into any one group's hands. Which phrase names fame and appeal spreading while the price of entry stays put?

More exclusive would mean the barriers ROSE -- that production got harder to reach than before. The prices in the story never moved: the software still costs nine hundred dollars, the same as always. Interest grew while access stood still.

Democratization means removing the barriers of cost and privilege so ordinary people can actually take part. Here the barriers never fell: the software still costs nine hundred dollars, equipment still runs thousands, and production stays 'as far out of reach for most people as ever.' Fame spreading while the door stays shut is popularization, not democratization -- democratization is what would finally open the door.

Monopolized would mean a single company or group seized control of music production and shut everyone else out. Nothing in the story hands production to one owner -- this is a story about attention soaring while prices simply stayed high.
